messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Private fleet: restore lifecycle & ops cadence for upcoming OS + runtime patching

Hi all,

We need a concrete ops cadence and a clear restore/undo lifecycle for the DataHealth private deployment ahead of the OS kernel + runtime (libmkl, CUDA drivers) patch next month. High level ask: sketch a schedule that minimizes customer downtime, defines canaries, preflight checks, and the exact rollback choreography (including who runs scripts, how we revoke pins, and required signals to abort).

Attached: preflight checklist, rollback scripts, and a proposed canary cohort matrix. Key constraints from DataHealth: 2-hour maintenance window (UTC 02:00-04:00), cross-datacenter private cloud (VPC peering between dc-eu-1 and dc-us-2), and zero-exposure SLA for production inference (they expect sub-250ms p95).

Proposed approach:
- Stage 0 (dry run): run preflight on staging with identical pin set and sample traffic replay (2 days prior).
- Stage 1 (canary): 5% traffic to canary cohort (pinned to new runtime) for 3 hours with automated telemetry checks.
- Stage 2 (phased rollout): 25% -> 60% -> full, with 1-hour soak between phases.
- If any phase fails health checks (latency, error-rate, kv-cache-miss spike), trigger backout as follows:
  1) Pause routing and drain canary via 30s graceful drain.
  2) Run rollback-scripts/restore_pin.sh to reapply previous model/runtime pin and restart serving processes on affected hosts.
  3) If restore_pin.sh fails, escalate to manual SSH-run of restore sequence (runbook: INF-4321) and open SEV bridge.

Decision points needed from this thread:
1) Ownership for canary monitoring and abort (suggest: Aditya ops lead, Neha as SRE owner).
2) Exact canary cohort (which AZs and node counts).
3) Signal thresholds (p95 latency + error rate + KV cache fill %).
4) Documentation and DocuSign approval for maintenance window with DataHealth.

Please review the checklist and the rollback scripts. I want a concrete, step-by-step runbook that someone on-call can execute without digging through other tickets. Aim to finalize by EOD Monday so we can schedule the dry run the week before the customer window.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Thanks Evelyn — good framing. A few quick clarifications and a small tweak to the cadence: 

1) Canary cohort: I recommend picking canaries only in dc-us-2 AZ-a and dc-eu-1 AZ-b (one AZ per region) to reduce blast radius and ensure we cover cross-region routing effects. Suggested node counts: 4 small-serving nodes in each AZ (total 8) to represent typical request distribution. I've attached an adjusted cohort matrix (see canary-cohort-matrix.xlsx).

2) Signals: propose abort thresholds as:
   - p95 latency increase > 20% over baseline for > 5 minutes
   - 5xx rate > 1% sustained for 3 minutes
   - KV cache miss % increase > 15% for 10 minutes
   - any client-reported authoritative failure (DataHealth)

3) Rollback timing: rollback-scripts/restore_pin.sh should be a fast-path operation (target full traffic restore in 12 minutes). If that completes, we still require a 30-minute soak to validate stability before continuing. If restore fails, open bridge and execute manual runbook.

4) Dry run scheduling: suggest dry run on Tue 2 days before their window, during their low-traffic period (we'll coordinate exact date with Sarah).

Small ask for Aditya: can you confirm that rebind-network.sh will maintain existing BGP advert weights and not create transient blackholes during drain? If not, we need a preflight BGP step.

Agree with Neha's thresholds and canary AZ selection. A couple implementation notes from the runtime/serving side:

- restore_pin.sh behavior: it re-writes the version pin file, triggers an orchestrator rolling restart (grace period 45s), and then signals the L7 router to re-evaluate route weights. It includes a ----force-fsync option for edge cases (use carefully).

- Network bind: rebind-network.sh only manipulates the application-level route weights and will not change BGP at the fabric level. ops-consultant@netops.io has an optional script re-teach-bgp.sh if we need control-plane level adjustments. That should be avoided unless we see packet loss.

- Telemetry hooks: I've added additional health checks to the canary pipeline: KV cache hit-rate, per-model token-generation time, and GPU SM utilization delta. All are pushed to the canary dashboard (link in INF ticket). We also added an automated job to compare a replayed golden prompt set against baseline output quality (fuzzy match threshold 0.95).

- Backout SLA: if restore_pin.sh completes but latency remains degraded, we will keep the pin and escalate to model-team rollback (re-pin model to previous checksum) — this is slower but necessary before considering network changes.

Next actions from me:
1) Drop the updated restore_pin.sh into the rollback-scripts bundle and add a verbose --dry-run option.
2) Create the canary dashboard and alert rules (will post link).
3) Coordinate dry-run date with Sarah.
